name: John C. Bennett
role: Nauvoo mayor and assistant president who turned critic
dateNote: He was baptized in September 1840, praised in section 124 in January 1841, and excommunicated on 11 May 1842.
importance: A physician and militia officer, Bennett helped secure the Nauvoo charter in 1840. Section 124 tells him to help Joseph Smith send the word abroad and promises reward “if he receive counsel”. He became mayor of Nauvoo and assistant president, then was excommunicated for adultery in 1842. He then accused Joseph Smith of adultery and of plotting the attack on Lilburn Boggs, which led to the hiding behind section 127.
connections: He worked with Joseph Smith and the Nauvoo city government. After leaving he aided Missouri and Illinois officials seeking Joseph’s arrest, and later joined James Strang’s movement for a time.

sources.title: John Cook Bennett, Joseph Smith Papers

reviewNote: Dates, baptism, Nauvoo offices, excommunication, accusations, exposé, and later moves checked on JSP. Accusations are reported as his claims; they are not stated as fact. The link to section 127 comes from that section’s setting.
